title: How is a clause that the platform carries out proved?
description: ST-DLV-UC05-R05 says that the platform's GitOps flow MUST run the environment check and that Argo CD MUST NOT apply an overlay whose check fails. ST-DLV-UC03-R06 and ST-DLV-PO03 say that the platform's gate MUST enforce the delivery policy that the pipeline carries. STEGO writes the check and the policy file, but the GitOps flow, Argo CD's sync and the gate are the platform's. Reading a: STEGO proves these clauses with a test of its own, against a reference platform that STEGO keeps as a fixture (a GitOps repository whose CI runs stego env check as a required check before Argo CD reads the branch, and a gate that evaluates the carried policy file), and STEGO also supplies that CI step or gate setting. Reading b: the clauses are the platform's obligations, which STEGO does not prove; STEGO proves only that the check fails and that the policy file is the one the check evaluates, and the records say that the platform provides the rest. Recommendation: reading b, with the platform's part recorded as provided by the platform, since ST-DLV-UC01 says the platform owns everything that comes from the environment, and a fixture of STEGO's own proves only the fixture. No test is written for ST-DLV-UC05-R05 or for the gate clauses until this is decided.

title: Does a verified compiler release move the pipeline pin directly, or only through a new ci-pipeline version?
description: ST-DLV-PO02 says that, when a published compiler release is verified, Write the delivery pipeline MUST read the verification record of the release and move the service's pipeline pin to that release. ST-DLV-INV04 and ST-DLV-UC04-R01 say that every pinned reference MUST come from the registry's ci-pipeline component. The two differ when the verified release is newer than the release the ci-pipeline component pins. Reading a: the policy reads the verification record and writes its pin into the CI file, and the ci-pipeline component does not pin the STEGO checks. Reading b: the policy moves the pin only when a platform engineer releases a ci-pipeline version that names the verified release, as the main path of ST-DLV-UC04 says; the verification record only lets that version be released. Recommendation: reading b, because it keeps one source for every pin, which ST-DLV-INV04 exists for, and the policy text then says that it waits for the new ci-pipeline version. No test is written for ST-DLV-PO02 until this is decided.

title: Does the import rule of a fill hold for its test files too?
description: ST-EXT-INV05 says that a fill's code MUST import only its slot's contract package, the Go standard library and the fill modules that the declaration lists. ST-EXT-UC01-R03 says that STEGO records no evidence for a fill that imports anything else. ST-EXT-UC04-R01 names a fill's code and its tests as two different things. Reading a: the rule holds for each Go file in the fill folder, test files too, so a test cannot import a test library such as testify unless the declaration lists it. Reading b: the rule holds for the files that are built into the service, and a test file can import any module that the project's go.mod holds. The test plan has no test of the imports of a test file until this is decided.

title: What is the contract package of one slot, when the generator writes every slot's contract into the one package out/slots?
description: ST-EXT-INV05 and ST-EXT-UC01-R03 let a fill import only its own slot's contract package. The generator writes the contracts of all slots into one Go package, out/slots, so a fill for before_create that imports out/slots can also use the types of before_delete. Reading a: out/slots is the contract package of each slot, and the import rule does not separate one slot from another. Reading b: the contract of each slot MUST be a package of its own, so that the import check can refuse the contract of another slot; this changes the generated layout. Reading c: the check reads the identifiers that a fill uses, not only its imports. The test plan tests imports outside out/slots only, until this is decided.

title: When two components of the active set declare a slot of one name, which fills does the list of fills for that name show?
description: stego registry fills takes --slot alone (ST-SUP-CLI06), and ST-EXT-UC03-R02 refuses a slot name that no component of the active set declares. stego fill create takes --component for a slot name that more than one component declares (ST-EXT-CLI01), so two components can declare one slot name. The fill catalog (ST-EXT-RM01) has no component field. Reading a: the list shows the fills of the slot of each such component, and each line names the component. Reading b: the list refuses the name as ambiguous, names the components that declare it, and takes --component as fill create does. The test plan has no test with two components that declare one slot name until this is decided.

title: Does a change to a .proto file that a slot contract imports make the slot's fills stale?
description: ST-EXT-DS01 computes the digest of a slot contract from the slot's .proto file alone. A slot's .proto file imports other files: before_create.proto of rest-api imports stego/common/types.proto, which defines CreateRequest and Identity. ST-EXT-UC04-R01 makes a fill stale when its slot contract changes. Reading a: the contract is the .proto file alone, so a change to types.proto leaves each fill qualified, although the messages that the fill reads change. Reading b: the contract digest MUST also cover each file that the slot's .proto file imports; this changes ST-EXT-DS01. The test plan tests ST-EXT-DS01 only with changes to files that the contract does not import, until this is decided.
